metadata.purpose: Take apart Anthropic's competitive-analysis skill: two files, a linear procedure, no hidden logic. Explain the machinery, name the trade-off (predictability vs. adaptiveness), and hand the viewer a paste-ready LLM prompt to poke at the design choice themselves.

beats.narration_text: Take this apart. You get a finished competitive-analysis deck out of Claude and you think Claude judged your market. It didn't. The skill executed a fixed procedure from a text file. Judging isn't processing. So which is actually happening?

beats.narration_text: Here's what a skill actually is: a folder Claude reads before it does anything. The competitive-analysis skill is two files — a SKILL.md and a references folder. The SKILL.md is the whole instruction set in plain English. No compiled binary, no hidden layer, nothing you can't open in a text editor. Claude reads it, then acts. They optimized for legibility over cleverness. The file is the program.

The pipeline lives in the Steps section. Claude reads SKILL.md, walks each step top to bottom, hands back the result. Linear by default — branching only where a step explicitly writes it in. That's the trade-off: predictability over adaptiveness. Same procedure every run.

production_viz.label: READ, EXECUTE, RETURN
production_viz.caption: linear — no branching unless a step says so

beats.narration_text: The skill's answering surface is exactly what SKILL.md specifies — no wider. Ask inside the scope — market map, peer comparison, positioning assessment — and you get the same procedure every run. Ask outside it and there's nothing in the file to execute. That's the cost of making the file the program: reliability inside the box, silence outside it.

production_viz.label: ONLY WHAT THE FILE SAYS
production_viz.caption: same input, same steps, every run

beats.narration_text: A skill runs the same steps on every request — read the file, execute in order, return the result. It only knows what's written in that file, nothing more.

props.quote: A skill runs the same steps on every request — read the file, execute in order, return the result. It only knows what's written in that file, nothing more.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: build a competitive landscape deck for three regional business-banking platforms, and have it read the competitive-analysis skill and walk you through the steps before it acts. Then check what actually happened — did it name the steps from the file, or did it improvise? That's the real test of whether the skill ran, or Claude went its own way.

props.command: Build a competitive landscape deck comparing three regional business-banking platforms I'm evaluating. Read the competitive-analysis skill and walk me through what you will do before you do it.

beats.narration_text: Here's a prompt you can paste directly into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini to think about skills as a design choice, not just this one skill. Go deeper: what would a skill system look like if it allowed conditional reasoning inside the file — and would that still count as a skill?

llm_exercise.prompt: I want to understand Anthropic's skill system as a design choice. A skill is a folder Claude reads before acting: a SKILL.md file with plain-language instructions plus optional references. The SKILL.md is the whole program — Claude reads it, executes each step in order, and returns the result; no branching unless a step writes it in. Give me three concrete cases where making the file the program helps (predictability, auditability, reuse), and two cases where it hurts (novel requests, adaptive judgment). For each case, name what was optimized for and what was sacrificed.
llm_exercise.dig_deeper: Go deeper: what would a skill system look like if it allowed conditional reasoning inside the file — and would that still count as a skill, or would it be something else?
